title: John Chapter 16 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on John chapter 16 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: John Chapter 16 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of John Chapter 16.

questions.question: In John 16, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: They shall put you out of the synagogues
These things have I spoken unto you
Nevertheless I tell you the truth
questions.correctAnswer: These things have I spoken unto you
questions.explanation: This is the first statement made in the chapter, found in John 16:1.

questions.question: What will happen to the followers according to John 16:2?
options: They shall put you out of the synagogues
questions.correctAnswer: They shall put you out of the synagogues
questions.explanation: This is stated directly in John 16:2.

questions.question: Why will they do these things to the followers according to John 16:3?
options: Because they have known the Father
Because they have not known the Father, nor me
questions.correctAnswer: Because they have not known the Father, nor me
questions.explanation: This is directly stated in John 16:3.

questions.question: What does Jesus say will happen when the time comes in John 16:4?
options: They will remember what he told them
questions.correctAnswer: They will remember what he told them
questions.explanation: This is the message in John 16:4.

questions.question: According to John 16:5, who is Jesus going to?
questions.explanation: Jesus mentions going to him that sent him, which is the Father, in John 16:5.

questions.question: What has filled the hearts of the followers in John 16:6?
questions.explanation: The text states that sorrow hath filled your heart in John 16:6.

questions.question: What is necessary for the Comforter to come according to John 16:7?
questions.explanation: John 16:7 states that it is expedient for you that I go away for the Comforter to come.

questions.question: What will the Comforter do when he comes according to John 16:8?
options: He will reprove the world of sin
questions.correctAnswer: He will reprove the world of sin
questions.explanation: This is stated in John 16:8.

questions.question: According to John 16:9, what is the reason for sin?
options: Because they believe not on me
questions.correctAnswer: Because they believe not on me
questions.explanation: This is the direct statement from John 16:9.

questions.question: Of what is the righteousness linked to according to John 16:10?
options: Because I go to my Father
questions.correctAnswer: Because I go to my Father
questions.explanation: This is what John 16:10 states about righteousness.

questions.question: What does John 16:11 say is judged?
questions.explanation: This is the information given in John 16:11.

questions.question: Is it true that Jesus said he was going to the Father in John 16?
questions.explanation: This is mentioned in John 16:5 where Jesus states he is going to him that sent him.

questions.question: Is it true that the Comforter will come after Jesus leaves according to John 16?
questions.explanation: Jesus states in John 16:7 that the Comforter will come if he departs.

questions.question: Is it false that sorrow filled the hearts of the disciples because of joy?
questions.explanation: Sorrow filled their hearts as stated in John 16:6, not joy.

questions.question: Is it false that the Comforter will judge the world according to John 16?
questions.explanation: The Comforter will reprove the world, not judge it, as stated in John 16:8.

medium.title: John Chapter 16 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from John Chapter 16 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does Jesus say He has yet to do in John 16:12?
questions.explanation: Jesus states in John 16:12, 'I have yet many things to say unto you, but ye cannot bear them now.' This indicates that there is more He wishes to communicate.

questions.question: What does John 16:13 promise will happen if someone receives the Spirit of truth?
options: They will be guided into all truth
They will be put out of synagogues
questions.correctAnswer: They will be guided into all truth
questions.explanation: John 16:13 states, 'Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth...' showing the promise of guidance.

questions.question: Who does the Spirit of truth glorify according to John 16:14?
questions.explanation: In John 16:14, it says, 'He shall glorify me: for he shall receive of mine, and shall shew it unto you,' indicating that the Spirit's role is to glorify Jesus.

questions.question: What does John 16:15 emphasize about the relationship between the Father and Jesus?
options: The Father is greater than Jesus
All things that the Father hath are Jesus's
Jesus does not know the Father
The Father and Jesus are in conflict
questions.correctAnswer: All things that the Father hath are Jesus's
questions.explanation: John 16:15 states, 'All things that the Father hath are mine...' showing the unity of possession between the Father and the Son.

questions.question: What does Jesus mean by saying 'A little while, and ye shall not see me' in John 16:16?
options: He is going to the Father forever
questions.explanation: John 16:16 indicates that Jesus will be with them again, implying a temporary absence.

questions.question: How did the disciples respond to Jesus's statement about seeing Him again in John 16:17?
options: They were confused and questioned among themselves
questions.correctAnswer: They were confused and questioned among themselves
questions.explanation: In John 16:17, it says, 'Then said some of his disciples among themselves, What is this that he saith unto us...' indicating their confusion.

questions.question: What does Jesus predict will happen to His disciples in John 16:20?
options: They will be put to death
They will be honored by the world
questions.explanation: In John 16:20, Jesus says, 'That ye shall weep and lament, but the world shall rejoice...' showing the emotional turmoil they will experience.

questions.question: What analogy does Jesus use in John 16:21 to describe the disciples' sorrow?
questions.explanation: In John 16:21, He mentions, 'A woman when she is in travail hath sorrow...' to illustrate the temporary nature of their sorrow.

questions.question: What promise does Jesus give in John 16:22 regarding their future joy?
options: No one can take their joy from them
They will have joy only after His return
Their joy will depend on the world
questions.correctAnswer: No one can take their joy from them
questions.explanation: John 16:22 states, '...and your joy no man taketh from you,' assuring them of enduring joy.

questions.question: What does John 16:6 reveal about the disciples' emotional state?
questions.explanation: In John 16:6, it states, '...sorrow hath filled your heart,' highlighting their distress over Jesus's words.

questions.question: What does John 16:7 say is necessary for the Comforter to come?
questions.explanation: John 16:7 states, 'It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you,' indicating His departure is essential.

questions.question: What will the Spirit of truth do when He comes, according to John 16:8?
questions.explanation: John 16:8 states, 'he will reprove the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment,' outlining the Spirit's mission.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus promised that their sorrow would be permanent.
questions.explanation: Jesus promises in John 16:20 that their sorrow will be turned into joy, indicating it is not permanent.

questions.question: True or False: The Spirit of truth will speak of Himself according to John 16:13.
questions.explanation: John 16:13 specifies that the Spirit 'shall not speak of himself; but whatsoever he shall hear, that shall he speak,' indicating He speaks what He hears.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus states that He will not see the disciples again after leaving them.
questions.explanation: In John 16:16, Jesus mentions, 'and again, a little while, and ye shall see me,' indicating He will return.

hard.title: John Chapter 16 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from John Chapter 16.

questions.question: What will the Father give you if you ask in Jesus' name?
questions.explanation: In John 16:23, Jesus states that whatsoever ye shall ask the Father in my name, he will give it you.

questions.question: What is the result of asking in Jesus' name according to John 16:24?
options: Your sorrow will turn to joy
questions.explanation: John 16:24 indicates that asking in Jesus' name leads to receiving, that your joy may be full.

questions.question: What does Jesus say will happen when He no longer speaks in proverbs?
options: He will show plainly of the Father
questions.correctAnswer: He will show plainly of the Father
questions.explanation: In John 16:25, Jesus mentions that He will show you plainly of the Father when the time comes.

questions.question: What does Jesus mean when He says, 'At that day ye shall ask in my name'?
questions.explanation: John 16:26 indicates that at that day, you shall ask in His name and not that He will pray for you.

questions.question: Why does Jesus say the Father loves you?
options: Because you have believed in Him
Because you ask in His name
questions.correctAnswer: Because you have believed in Him
questions.explanation: John 16:27 explains that the Father loves you because you have loved Jesus and believed that He came from God.

questions.question: What does Jesus say about the hour that is coming?
questions.explanation: In John 16:32, Jesus warns that the hour is coming when you shall be scattered and leave Him alone.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'ask' in John 16:23 mean?
questions.explanation: The Greek word for 'ask' implies making a request, aligning with the context of prayer in John 16:23.

questions.question: Which literary device is used in John 16:33 when Jesus says 'be of good cheer; I have overcome the world'?
questions.explanation: This statement foreshadows Jesus' victory over sin and death, indicating future triumph for believers.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects with the theme of being scattered in John 16:32?
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:7 speaks of striking the shepherd and the sheep being scattered, echoing the scattering Jesus predicts.

questions.question: Which passage in Revelation connects with the promise of peace in John 16:33?
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:4 speaks of God wiping away tears and providing peace, connecting to the peace Jesus offers in John 16:33.

questions.question: What comes before Jesus' statement about being scattered in John 16:32?
questions.explanation: John 16:32 follows Jesus' warning about tribulation, leading into the discussion of being scattered.

questions.question: What does John 16:2 imply about the future treatment of Jesus' followers?
questions.explanation: John 16:2 indicates that followers will be put out of synagogues and even killed, implying persecution.

questions.question: What does John 16:20 say about the disciples' emotions after Jesus' departure?
questions.explanation: John 16:20 states that the disciples will weep and lament while the world rejoices, highlighting their sorrow.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus promises that the Father will not hear your requests if you do not ask in His name.
questions.explanation: John 16:23 emphasizes that requests must be made in Jesus' name for the Father to grant them.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus assures His disciples that they will never face tribulation in the world.
questions.explanation: In John 16:33, Jesus clearly states that in the world, His followers shall have tribulation.

theological.title: John Chapter 16 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from John Chapter 16 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does John 16:7 teach about the role of the Comforter in the believer's sanctification?
options: The Comforter convicts believers of sin to encourage repentance
The Comforter only acts after Jesus returns physically
The Comforter is sent only to the unbelieving world
The Comforter is sent because Jesus departs, to aid believers
questions.correctAnswer: The Comforter is sent because Jesus departs, to aid believers
questions.explanation: John 16:7 explains it is expedient for Jesus to go away so that He may send the Comforter to believers, indicating the Comforter's role in sanctification after Jesus' departure.

questions.question: What doctrine about human sin is revealed in John 16:9 regarding the world's condition?
options: Sin is primarily ignorance of the Law
Sin is unbelief in Jesus as the Christ
Sin is the result of physical death
Sin is a social construct rather than a spiritual reality
questions.correctAnswer: Sin is unbelief in Jesus as the Christ
questions.explanation: John 16:9 states sin is because they believe not on Jesus, revealing the doctrine that unbelief constitutes sin.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning Christ’s exaltation and its effect on believers is taught in John 16:10?
options: Christ's going to the Father establishes His righteousness
Christ’s ascension nullifies His priestly intercession
Christ’s exaltation means believers must earn righteousness
Christ’s return to the Father ends all revelation to believers
questions.correctAnswer: Christ's going to the Father establishes His righteousness
questions.explanation: John 16:10 explains the Spirit reproves the world of righteousness because Jesus goes to the Father, indicating the doctrine that Christ’s exaltation confirms His righteousness.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does John 16:8 specifically demonstrate in the work of the Spirit?
questions.explanation: John 16:8 states the Spirit will reprove the world of sin, righteousness, and judgment, demonstrating God's attribute of judicial authority through the Spirit.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is underscored by Jesus’ statement in John 16:28 about His origin and return?
questions.explanation: John 16:28 emphasizes Jesus’ coming forth from the Father and return to Him, affirming His eternal existence and divine nature.

questions.question: How does John 16:20–22 connect to the broader biblical theme of suffering and glory?
options: It parallels the Exodus journey from slavery to freedom
It prefigures the resurrection hope and joy after suffering
It emphasizes the final judgment of the wicked
It shows the temporary nature of the Law’s condemnation
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures the resurrection hope and joy after suffering
questions.explanation: John 16:20–22 uses the metaphor of a woman in childbirth whose pain turns to joy, connecting to the biblical theme of suffering followed by resurrection joy.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection is highlighted by Jesus’ promise in John 16:13 that the Spirit will guide into all truth?
options: The fulfillment of Old Testament prophecy about the Spirit
The inauguration of the Mosaic covenant
The establishment of the Davidic monarchy
The end of the priestly system
questions.correctAnswer: The fulfillment of Old Testament prophecy about the Spirit
questions.explanation: John 16:13’s promise of the Spirit guiding into all truth fulfills Old Testament prophecies (e.g., Isaiah 11:2) about the coming Spirit of truth.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do John 16:23 and John 16:24 teach about prayer and divine providence?
options: Believers must first ask the Father directly, not through Jesus
Prayer in Jesus’ name guarantees fullness of joy through answered petitions
Prayer is optional since God’s will is always done
Only the apostles have the authority to pray in Jesus’ name
questions.correctAnswer: Prayer in Jesus’ name guarantees fullness of joy through answered petitions
questions.explanation: John 16:23-24 teaches that asking the Father in Jesus’ name results in receiving, which fills believers’ joy, affirming the doctrine of effective prayer in Christ’s name.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do John 16:12 and John 16:13 reveal about the Spirit’s teaching ministry?
options: The Spirit will reveal new truth independent of Jesus
The Spirit will only remind believers of Old Testament law
The Spirit will guide into all truth by speaking what He hears from Jesus
The Spirit’s role is limited to convicting unbelievers
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit will guide into all truth by speaking what He hears from Jesus
questions.explanation: John 16:12-13 shows Jesus has more to teach but the Spirit will come to guide believers into all truth by speaking what He hears from Jesus, emphasizing the Spirit’s dependent teaching ministry.

questions.question: What combined doctrine is taught by John 16:32 and John 16:33 about Christ’s presence amid suffering?
options: Christ will abandon believers in trials
Believers will face tribulation, but Christ’s abiding presence with the Father brings peace
Christ’s presence guarantees a life without tribulation
Peace is only found after the final judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Believers will face tribulation, but Christ’s abiding presence with the Father brings peace
questions.explanation: John 16:32-33 teaches that although believers will be scattered and face tribulation, Christ is not alone because the Father is with Him, and believers can have peace in Him despite trials.

questions.question: Sceptics claim John 16:7–11 promotes a doctrine where the Spirit condemns the world arbitrarily. What does this passage actually teach?
options: The Spirit reproves the world on the basis of sin, righteousness, and judgment related to Jesus
The Spirit condemns the world for its cultural differences
The Spirit’s role is to punish unbelievers without warning
The Spirit’s reproof is limited to believers only
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit reproves the world on the basis of sin, righteousness, and judgment related to Jesus
questions.explanation: John 16:7–11 clarifies that the Spirit reproves based on specific grounds: sin is unbelief in Jesus, righteousness comes from Jesus going to the Father, and judgment because the prince of this world is judged, not arbitrary condemnation.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine love is expressed in John 16:27?
options: The Father’s love is conditional upon human merit
The Father loves believers because they have loved Jesus and believed His divine origin
Divine love is unrelated to faith in Christ
The Father’s love is only for the Jewish people
questions.correctAnswer: The Father loves believers because they have loved Jesus and believed His divine origin
questions.explanation: John 16:27 states the Father loves believers because they have loved Jesus and believed He came from God, teaching the doctrine of reciprocal divine love grounded in faith.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is particularly demonstrated in Jesus’ statement in John 16:31 concerning His disciples’ belief?
questions.explanation: In John 16:31, Jesus questions the disciples' belief, demonstrating His omniscience by knowing their doubts and understanding their hearts.

questions.question: How does John 16:4 fit into the narrative arc of Jesus preparing His disciples for future persecution and separation?
options: It shows Jesus was unaware of future events
It reveals Jesus’ prior teaching aimed to prepare disciples for coming trials
It denies any future suffering for believers
It focuses only on the miracles Jesus performed
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals Jesus’ prior teaching aimed to prepare disciples for coming trials
questions.explanation: John 16:4 shows Jesus told the disciples beforehand about coming persecution so that they would remember His words when it occurred, preparing them for trials ahead.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do John 16:25 and John 16:29 provide about Jesus’ revelation to His disciples?
options: Jesus will continue to speak only in parables
Jesus promises to speak plainly about the Father, no longer in proverbs
Jesus’ teaching will become more obscure over time
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus promises to speak plainly about the Father, no longer in proverbs
questions.explanation: John 16:25 and John 16:29 together reveal that Jesus had previously spoken in proverbs but now speaks plainly about the Father, signifying a clearer revelation to the disciples.
